title: Open a Leatherman multitool's pliers: swing both handles half a turn round their pivots until they click home
instruction: Open the pliers out of the multitool, ready to use, and leave it on the desk.
context: A folding multitool's pliers are opened every time the tool is used, and Leatherman alone had sold more than 20 million of them by 2001. Closed, the plier head sits inside the two handles. Each handle has to swing half a turn about its own pivot, the two in opposite directions, until they meet back to back and click home. The tool lies loose on the desk, so pushing one handle round on its own drags the whole tool along unless the other hand holds it still.
setup: Desk top at the station's table height; positions are from the arms' base line (x forward, y to the robot's left). One Leatherman Wave+ multitool (stainless steel, 241 g): closed 102 x 38 x 18 mm, lying flat on its large face, closed, its pivot end towards the robot. The midpoint of its two handle pivots is at x 30.0 cm, y 0, and the closed handles' free ends point away from the robot (to x 39.2 cm). Each handle (85 g) is 19 mm wide and 18 mm thick, 92 mm from its pivot to its free end, rounded about the pivot at its other end; the pivots are 19 mm apart, 9.5 mm from the pivot end. The plier head (71 g, jaws shut) is 68 mm from the pivot line to the jaw tip, 25 mm wide at the pivots, 9 mm thick, and lies inside the two closed handles. Opening swings the right-hand handle (as the robot sees it) clockwise and the left-hand one anticlockwise, half a turn each about its own pivot; open, the handles lie back to back on the robot's side of the head and the tool is 160 mm long. Each pivot has a detent that holds the handle shut through its first 12 degrees (about 0.01 N m to start it, 0.03 N m at 12 degrees) and pulls it home onto its open stop through its last 40 degrees, and about 0.008 N m of friction between. Distractors, which the score ignores: a ceramic mug (11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 300 g) at x 50 cm, y 21 cm; a pair of glasses (14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 30 g) at x 53 cm, y -20 cm; a tape dispenser (15.9 x 6.4 x 6.6 cm, 350 g) at x 57.5 cm, y 0, its long side across the desk. Both grippers start open in the raised ready pose, well clear of the tool.
scoring: Read from the state at each step; only a fall is remembered. 1.0: both handles swung round to their open stops (each more than 170 degrees from shut, and the two handles' free ends no more than 2 mm apart, back to back), the tool lying flat on the desk (its underside within 3 mm of the desk, tilted 5 degrees or less), every fingertip at least 30 mm from the tool, and all of this held still for 1 s (20 steps). 0.5: both handles swung at least 90 degrees from shut (the jaws clear of both handles), without the full conditions. 0.25: one handle swung at least 90 degrees from shut. 0: anything else, including the start. 0 also if the tool has fallen off the desk at any time in the trial.
reset_notes: Fold each handle back over the plier head until its detent holds it shut, lay the tool flat on its tape outline with the pivot end towards the robot, and open both grippers in the ready pose. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: The Wave+ is modelled from its published outer dimensions as rigid parts: two solid handles (the blades and inside tools are not modelled) and one plier head with its jaws fixed shut; only the two handle pivots move. The detent springs and pivot friction are estimates, not measurements. PhysX averages two materials per contact, so the tool's faces carry values that give rubber pad on steel 0.95 and steel on desk 0.35. Distractors are SimReady props.
